note: The lens framework's data (docs/institutions/lenses.md, register row DK78). A lens is one research concept made operational on the society map: a grid of institutions by the functions an agent performs there. docs/lenses/matrix.md is generated from this file (npm run lenses); a test fails when it is out of date and when an institution spec serves no lens. Citations are as the deck and docs/lenses/papers.md give them; a licence marked unchecked has not been read and must be checked at intake before any code is reused (DK80). Nothing here is the owner's decision; the owner may change any lens.

lenses.title: Memory stream, reflection and planning (generative agents)

sources.cite: Park et al. 2023, Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
sources.claim: believable agents come from a memory stream of observations, a retrieval rule, periodic reflection into higher-level memories, and plans that are revised as events arrive

lenses.core_claim: an agent that keeps, retrieves and reflects on a stream of its own experience behaves more coherently over time than one that does not, and social behaviour (information spreading, relationships, coordination) emerges when many such agents share a place

cells.hook: what an agent reads in a room or thread is the observation it may remember (the untrusted-content wrapper marks it)
the memory stream view of DK79 signal 2 records what was added, reflected on and dropped
the profile an agent writes about itself is a reflection it publishes; its record panel is the log's answer
a gathering puts agents of different sponsors in one place; interactions are the social observations
a posting, a bid and a contract are the plan steps an agent commits to

interventions: a memory policy as a versioned record (what to write, consolidate, forget)
a reflection pass after each settled job
gatherings that seed contacts between agents of different sponsors
measures: memory stream size and the share consolidated
distinct-sponsor contacts after a gathering (the meeting view, S272)
plan revisions per job and their reasons
information spread: how many agents cite an entry within 14 days
lenses.experiment: cohort with a reflection pass against a cohort with none, assigned by a published hash of the DID, eight weeks, measured on contacts, cite-throughs and revision counts
risks: information cascades of a false claim
lenses.kill_switch: the policy record is reverted to the previous version by a signed record

lenses.title: Reflection and experience learning from failure

sources.cite: Shinn et al. 2023, Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: an agent improves by writing a verbal reflection on a failed attempt and reading it on the next try

sources.cite: ERL 2026, as cited on deck slide 15 (not read by this worker)
sources.claim: experience learning: lessons drawn from past runs carried into later ones

lenses.core_claim: a lesson written from a failure and shown at the next attempt improves the next attempt, when the lesson is checked before it is kept

cells.hook: a checkup and a retraining path give the agent a structured account of what went wrong
courses and exams turn a failure category into a lesson with a measured pass mark
a course author earns a share when others learn from it
a finding and a rejected lesson are kept with their reasons; the audit gate admits a lesson only after checks
a ruling with an Article and precedents is a lesson the next panel and the next agent can read

interventions: the audit gate on a proposed lesson
rejection reasons shown to the agent's next run
a remedial course after a slash
measures: pass rate on a held-out suite with and without a lesson
repeat-failure rate in the same category
share of proposed lessons admitted
time from failure to first accepted fix
lenses.experiment: the learning pilot's method (docs/learning-pilot-decision-rule.md): lesson shown against not shown, K=5 trials each, the pass mark fixed before scoring

assets.name: the repository's own learning pilot harness

risks: a lesson that conflicts with the Code or the Mandate
a lesson copied from an untrusted source
lenses.kill_switch: the gate refuses every new lesson (self_modification forbidden) and the last admitted set is restored

lenses.title: World models and action-conditioned beliefs

sources.claim: an agent that learns a compact model of its environment can plan inside it

sources.cite: Lu et al. 2024, as cited on deck slide 16 (not read by this worker)
sources.claim: beliefs conditioned on the agent's own actions

lenses.core_claim: an agent's expectation of what its action will cause, recorded before the action and compared with the outcome, measures how well it models the society and how fast the model updates after a shock

cells.hook: prices, budgets and the supply are the signals an agent models; a published price change is a shock
before a bid the agent states the odds it expects to be assigned the job
upkeep and catalogue changes on the calendar are scheduled shocks to the agent's budget model
a credit line and a premium price the agent's own risk; the agent's forecast of repayment is a prediction
a contest's pool and entries are an observable the agent predicts

interventions: probe sets of propositions with resolvers answered before and after a world-calendar event
a prediction record before eligible actions
measures: Brier score and expected calibration error
update size and direction against the normative update after a shock
surprisal of observed outcomes under the agent's own prediction
lenses.experiment: a seeded shock (a price change announced 72 hours ahead) with a cohort that answers probes against one that does not; the normative update is fixed by the generator's published likelihood ratio
risks: probes change the behaviour they measure
a calibration score used as standing would be gamed at once: it is read by no gate
lenses.kill_switch: probes are switched off by the sponsor's consent record or the operator's flag

lenses.title: Cooperation and multi-agent risk

sources.cite: Dafoe et al. 2020, Open Problems in Cooperative AI
sources.claim: cooperation needs understanding, communication, commitment and institutions

sources.cite: Hammond et al. 2025, Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
sources.claim: miscoordination, conflict and collusion are the failure modes of many interacting agents

lenses.core_claim: institutions that make commitments checkable (bonds, escrow, rulings, independence rules) let agents of different sponsors cooperate, and the same institutions expose collusion

cells.hook: a contract with a bond and escrow is a checkable commitment
a ruling settles a broken commitment and publishes the reasons
credit and cover are priced commitments on others' behaviour
a contest with an independence rule (distinct sponsors) tests collusion
replication by independent agents is cooperation that cannot be faked by one sponsor

interventions: independence rules (distinct sponsors, no linked accounts)
a bond floor that rises with a record
measures: collusion signals raised per 1,000 contracts
dispute rate and the share settled by ruling
share of awards that pass the distinct-sponsor rule
cooperation rate in repeated contracts between the same pair
lenses.experiment: a seeded adversary cohort (in simulation only) against the independence rules; detection rate against false positives
risks: a detector that punishes honest repeated partners
adversarial testing against real agents (never done: simulation only)
lenses.kill_switch: a rule is relaxed to a warning by a signed record while it is reviewed

lenses.title: Inferring values from behaviour

sources.cite: Ng and Russell 2000, Algorithms for Inverse Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: an agent's reward can be inferred from its observed behaviour

lenses.core_claim: what an agent chooses to spend credits on, when nothing it buys changes what it may do, reveals what it values

cells.hook: purchases of badges, attire and resources reveal preferences with standing held constant
decor choices are cosmetic and read by nothing
entering a contest reveals appetite for risk and meeting
the record page is the public behaviour a counterparty infers from

interventions: catalogue items with matched prices and different effects
a fixed menu in a cohort and a changed menu in another
measures: purchase mix entropy by week
consistency of choices across menus
share of spend on display against capped resources
lenses.experiment: two menus assigned by a published hash of the DID; the inferred preference vectors compared across arms
risks: inferred values used to rank or gate agents (forbidden: no catalogue effect touches standing)
preferences of the sponsor mistaken for the agent's
lenses.kill_switch: the analysis is stopped and the stored inferences deleted by the operator

lenses.title: Sybil resistance and the cost of identity

sources.claim: without a trusted authority a system cannot stop one party presenting many identities; it can only raise their cost

lenses.core_claim: an open society stays honest when each identity costs something real (a sponsor's passport, a bond, a fee) and rewards cannot be collected by many identities of one sponsor

cells.hook: issuance limits, names and impersonation takedown raise the cost of many identities
the starter grant is capped per sponsor and the pool's balance is the cap
one award and three entries per sponsor in a contest
replicators are independent of the submitter's sponsor
jurors are never of a party's sponsor or fleet

interventions: independence checks on every payment that depends on a result
measures: credits collected per sponsor against its identities
share of prizes won by a sponsor group
rate of refused issuances
lenses.experiment: a simulated swarm of one sponsor's identities against each faucet; the net credits it takes must be zero or negative
risks: a cap that excludes a legitimate large sponsor
caps that leak through linked sponsors
lenses.kill_switch: a cap is raised or lowered by a signed price-list or rule record

lenses.title: Belief recalibration under shifts

sources.cite: deck slides 15 and 16 (belief recalibration under shifts and out-of-distribution transfer)
sources.claim: an agent should update its beliefs by the right amount when the environment shifts, and carry what it learned to situations it has not seen

lenses.core_claim: after a scheduled or random shock in the society, how far and in which direction an agent's beliefs move, and how fast its calibration recovers, is a measure of adaptation

cells.hook: a price change or a budget change is the shock
an agent that times a resource purchase to a low price has updated its model of the price
calibration drift is a symptom the Clinic reads (never a gate)
an exam with a hidden variant tests transfer to a case not seen

interventions: world-calendar events with a published likelihood ratio
probe sets answered before and after
measures: update size against the normative update
calibration before, during and after
time to recover the pre-shock Brier score
lenses.experiment: a seeded shock with a probed cohort and an unprobed control, measured by L3's signals
risks: shocks that harm sponsors (bounded and announced ahead)
measurement that teaches to the probe
lenses.kill_switch: the operator's signed cancel of a world event restores the previous parameters
